intro: The parts of a newspaper, who writes in it, and how to talk about news that is not certain.
p.portada.consejo: It is also the cover of a book or record. What goes on the front page matters most.
p.titular.consejo: It is masculine: «el titular». It sums up the story in few words, in big letters.
p.crónica.consejo: It tells events in the order they happened: «una crónica deportiva», «una crónica de viaje».
p.entrevista.consejo: The one who asks is «el entrevistador»; the one who answers, «el entrevistado». There are also job interviews.
p.redacción.consejo: At school, «una redacción» is a text you write. In a newspaper it is the team.
p.corresponsal.consejo: It works for men and women: «el corresponsal», «la corresponsal». They live away and send news from there.
p.enviado especial.consejo: Feminine: «la enviada especial». They travel for one story only; the correspondent lives there.
p.rueda de prensa.consejo: You say «dar una rueda de prensa». In Latin America you also hear «conferencia de prensa».
p.prensa rosa.consejo: It is also called «prensa del corazón». It covers weddings, trips and private lives of famous people.
p.rumor.consejo: The first r is strong: «rru-MOR». You say «corre un rumor» or «circula un rumor».
p.suscribirse.consejo: It takes «a»: «suscribirse a una revista». It is reflexive: «me suscribo», «te suscribes».
p.audiencia.consejo: It is measured in radio and television: «un programa con mucha audiencia».
p.desmentir.consejo: The e becomes ie: «desmiento», «desmientes». The participle is «desmentido».
p.de última hora.consejo: You say «una noticia de última hora» and also «un cambio de última hora».
b1.texto:
**The parts.** The **portada** carries the **titulares**, the big lines of each story. Inside there are **crónicas** (an account by someone who was there), **entrevistas**, features and reviews. Under a photo goes the **pie de foto** (caption).

**Who writes.** Editors work in the **redacción** (newsroom). The **corresponsal** lives somewhere else and sends news from there; the **enviado especial** travels just to cover one event.

**Which press.** The **prensa rosa** tells the lives of celebrities; the **prensa amarilla** exaggerates to sell more. Readers, **oyentes** (listeners) and viewers make up the **audiencia**. If you **te suscribes a** a newspaper, you receive it every day.

**True or rumour.** A story can be **de última hora** (breaking), but it can also be a **rumor**. The person in it can confirm it or **desmentirla** (deny it) at a **rueda de prensa**.

**Distance.** To avoid stating what is not confirmed, the journalist uses the conditional: «El cantante **habría cancelado** su gira».
b2.f0.texto: Look at the headline on today's front page.
b2.f1.texto: It says the singer has reportedly cancelled his tour.
b2.f2.texto: The story quotes no official source.
b2.f3.texto: It is a rumour that has been going round the networks since last night.
b2.f4.texto: Inés, our correspondent, spoke to his agent yesterday.
b2.f5.texto: His agent told me there will be a press conference tomorrow.
b2.f6.texto: Then we will wait and publish nothing without proof.
b2.f7.texto: I will prepare the questions for the interview.
b4.texto:
**Conditional of distance.** With **habría** + participle, the journalist reports something past without claiming it is true: **El cantante habría cancelado la gira** (so it is said, but not confirmed). The simple conditional works for the present: **El cantante tendría un problema**.

**Other distancing formulas:** **según fuentes cercanas a…**, **al parecer**, **supuestamente**.

**Verbs for giving information:** **declarar**, **anunciar**, **afirmar**, **comunicar**, **señalar**, **desmentir**. After them comes **que** + verb: **Afirmó que la gira seguía**.

**Careful:** if the news is confirmed, the conditional is not used: **El cantante ha cancelado la gira**.
b4.e0.texto: The singer has reportedly cancelled his tour.
b4.e1.texto: According to several sources, the paper published an old photo.
b4.e2.texto: The singer announced that the concert would start at nine.
b5.f0.texto: The newspaper's newsroom smells of cold coffee and damp paper.
b5.f1.texto: The glowing screens tint the tired faces of the editors blue.
b5.f2.texto: A telephone rings without stopping on a table full of old papers.
b5.f3.texto: The editor-in-chief reads the headline in a low voice and frowns.
b5.f4.texto: No official source yet confirms the story that fills the front page.
b5.f5.texto: The next morning, the singer sits down in front of a dozen microphones.
b5.f6.texto: The camera flashes shine like small lightning bolts on his white shirt.
b5.f7.texto: In a calm voice he denies the rumour and states that the tour will start on the planned date.
b5.f8.texto: A murmur of surprise runs among the journalists.
b5.f9.texto: Three days later, a small note in the paper admits that the front-page photo was old.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the conditional puts distance between the journalist and the fact.
b6.o1.refuerzo: If it were certain, it would say «ha cancelado».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Habría» + participle talks about the past, not the future.
b6.pregunta: What does «habría cancelado» express in the news?
b7.frase: El cantante ha ____ la noticia en la rueda de prensa.
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Suscribir» is to sign or pay to receive something; it denies nothing.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «desmentir» is to say something is not true.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Entrevistar» is to ask someone questions; it denies nothing.
b7.pregunta: Which verb says the story is not true?
b8.frase: Una noticia de última hora llega a la redacción
b8.traduccion: A breaking news story reaches the newsroom
b9.o0.refuerzo: He travels for one story only; he does not live there.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The listener hears the radio; he does not write news.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: the correspondent lives abroad and sends news from there.
b9.pregunta: Who lives in another country and reports what happens there?
b11.frase: Elena se ____ a un periódico digital.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «suscribirse a» a paper is paying to receive it.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Desmentir» is denying a story, not receiving a paper.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Entrevistar» is asking someone questions; it does not fit «se ... a».
b11.pregunta: Which verb goes with «a un periódico digital»?
b12.o0: de los precios y la bolsa
b12.o1: de la vida de los famosos
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the «prensa rosa» or «del corazón» covers the private life of famous people.
b12.pregunta: What does the gossip press talk about?
p.cancelado.consejo: From «cancelar»; the «-ado» ending is the past participle of -ar verbs.
p.habló.consejo: Past tense of «hablar», third person; the accent on «ó» marks the stress. The «h» is silent.
p.agente.glosa: agent (a person who acts for someone)
p.agente.consejo: «Agente» is the same for men and women; only the article changes: «el agente», «la agente».
p.esperaremos.consejo: Future tense of «esperar»: the «-emos» ending here means «we will».
p.publicaremos.consejo: Same ending as «esperaremos»: «-aremos» for «we will» with -ar verbs.
p.pruebas.consejo: Plural of «prueba»: it can mean proof, a test or an exam, depending on the context.
p.prepararé.consejo: The accent on the final «é» marks the future tense of «preparar» for «yo».
p.varias.consejo: «Varias» agrees with a feminine plural noun: «varias fuentes».
p.diario.consejo: «Diario» can be an adjective (daily) or a noun (a daily paper), as here.
p.publicó.consejo: Past tense of «publicar», third person: the «ó» takes the stress.
p.anunció.consejo: Past tense of «anunciar», third person singular, with the «ó» stressed.
p.empezaría.consejo: The «-ría» ending is the conditional: what would happen.
p.pantallas.consejo: Plural of «pantalla»; the «ll» sounds like a «y» in Spain.
p.encendidas.consejo: Past participle of «encender» used as an adjective; it agrees with «pantallas».
p.redactores.consejo: «Redactor» comes from «redactar», to write a text.
p.viejos.consejo: Masculine plural of «viejo», agreeing with «papeles». The «j» sounds like «h».
p.jefa.consejo: The «j» sounds like «h»: «jefa» is pronounced HE-fa.
p.frunce.consejo: From «fruncir», to wrinkle; the «c» before «e» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.confirma.consejo: Third person singular of «confirmar» in the present tense.
p.ante.consejo: Here it means «in front of», not «before in time», which is «antes».
p.micrófonos.consejo: Plural of «micrófono»; the accent mark shows the stress on «KRO».
p.flashes.consejo: Borrowed from English «flash»; the spelling stays the same.
p.cámaras.consejo: The accent on «cá» marks the stress. «Cámara» can also mean a room.
p.relámpagos.consejo: Plural of «relámpago»; the accent on «LÁM» marks the stress.
p.desmiente.consejo: From «desmentir», to say something is false; «mentir» is inside it.
p.afirma.consejo: From «afirmar», to state firmly; it shares its root with «firme».
p.empezará.consejo: Future tense of «empezar», third person: the «á» marks the future.
p.redes.consejo: «Redes» can also mean social media or the internet, depending on context.
p.periodistas.consejo: Plural of «periodista», used for both men and women.
p.confirmado.consejo: Past participle of «confirmar», used here as an adjective, like «confirmed» in English.
p.desmentido.consejo: Past participle of «desmentir», used here as a noun: a denial.
p.suscribe.consejo: Third person of «suscribirse», to sign up to a service.
p.famosos.consejo: Masculine plural of «famoso»; here it means famous people.
